newsitem.title: UK: Pilkington says plans further price rises.
newsitem.headline: Pilkington says plans further price rises.

text.p: Pilkington Plc said on Thursday that it hoped to raise its glass prices in the course of the year as part of a strategy to boost the group's operating margins.

"We raised prices (by 20 percent) in April and this has been partially successful. I would expect further price rises in the course of the year, particularly in the summer when demand is at its peak," finance director Andrew Robb told Reuters in an interview.
Pilkington also pledged to trim overheads that top one billion stg worldwide, making these targets achievable -- with or without higher prices.
"Last year we didn't make money from building products in Germany. I'm fairly certain that some of our competitors did and I am fairly certain that we can, even at these prices," Robb said.
"This does mean that quite a lot of costs are going to come out."
Pilkington appointed Paolo Scaroni chief executive in May with a mandate to slash costs and said that it expected him to accelerate the pace of change within the group.

Robb said that with the new chief in the job for only 15 days it was too early to detail specific initiatives. But he warned the measures would have to be stringent and signalled Pilkington's layers of middle management could expect some tough action.
Pilkington is burdened with the "residue of an old regional organisation" and these subsidiary headquarters would be rationalised, Robb said.
He said that decisions over the headquarters would be taken within the next four weeks, with action following by year-end.
The company earlier posted pre-tax profits of 132 million stg -- down from 212 million and in the middle of market expectations following a profit warning in March.
